dpVersionModal.doubtfulDisclaimer: DP may still be secondary to another analysis method depending on the recurrence shape.
dpVersionModal.mainChangesText: This DP version replaces recursive calls with a bottom-up iterative approach. Instead of recursively computing subproblems (which may repeat multiple times), a table/matrix is built that stores subproblem results from base cases to the original problem. Each value is computed once and reused when needed, eliminating redundant recalculations that cause exponential complexity in the recursive version.
dpVersionModal.dpEquivalenceDefault: The roots of the characteristic equation correspond to the eigenvalues of the linear transition of the DP system. The closed-form mathematical solution is equivalent to the iterative solution via dynamic programming.
dpVersionModal.noRecalc: No recalculations: Each subproblem is solved only once
dpVersionModal.bottomUp: Bottom-up: Iterative construction from base cases

manualMode.defaultCode:
binarySearch(A[n], x, start, high) BEGIN
  IF (start > high) THEN BEGIN
    RETURN -1;
  END
  mid <- (start + high) / 2;
  IF (A[mid] = x) THEN BEGIN
    RETURN mid;
  END
  ELSE BEGIN
    IF (x < A[mid]) THEN BEGIN
      RETURN binarySearch(A, x, start, mid - 1);
    END
    ELSE BEGIN
      RETURN binarySearch(A, x, mid + 1, high);
    END
  END
END

about.title: About - AALIE
about.heroDesc: A modern educational tool for analyzing algorithmic complexity of pseudocode with interactive visualizations and automatic calculations.
about.whatDoesDesc: Takes your pseudocode, builds its structure with a formal grammar and automatically calculates the computational cost line by line. Generates T(n) formulas for best and worst case with control flow visualizations.
about.featureRecursiveDesc: Master Theorem, Iteration Method, Recursion Tree and Characteristic Equation with automatic detection
about.featureTraceDesc: Step-by-step visualization with React Flow for iterative algorithms and tree diagrams for recursive ones
about.featureLlmDesc: Analysis validation with Gemini 2.5 Pro, independent comparison and discrepancy detection
about.featureGpuDesc: Scoring system (0-100) that determines algorithm suitability for GPU or CPU based on parallelism and access patterns
about.featureVizDesc: Flow diagrams with React Flow, recursion trees, interactive AST and detailed cost tables
about.featureMemoDesc: Intelligent AST analysis cache, nested loop optimization and computational complexity reduction
about.noSignupDesc: No accounts required, no personal data stored
about.step1Desc: Enter your pseudocode in the editor
about.contactDesc: Have questions, suggestions or found an issue? Feel free to contact us

userGuide.title: User Guide
userGuide.subtitle: Learn to use the algorithmic complexity analyzer with this complete guide covering from basic syntax to advanced algorithm analysis.
userGuide.introDesc1: Welcome to the algorithmic complexity analyzer. This tool allows you to write algorithms in pseudocode and automatically obtain the analysis of their temporal complexity (Big O).
userGuide.introDesc2: The system uses a structured pseudocode language that is easy to read and write, with real-time validation and automatic suggestions to help you write correct code.
userGuide.introTipDescPre: If you're new, start by reviewing the
userGuide.introTipDescPost: to familiarize yourself with the syntax.
userGuide.editorBasicDesc: The editor is based on Monaco Editor (the same editor as Visual Studio Code) and offers advanced features:
userGuide.editorBasic1: Syntax highlighting specific to the pseudocode language
userGuide.editorBasic2: Keyword autocomplete (BEGIN, END, FOR, WHILE, etc.)
userGuide.editorValidDesc: The editor validates your code as you type, showing errors and warnings immediately:
userGuide.editorValid1: Red underline: Syntax errors that must be corrected
userGuide.editorValid2: Yellow underline: Warnings or improvement suggestions
userGuide.editorValid3: Descriptive messages when hovering over the error
userGuide.editorValid4: Indicators in the left margin for severe errors
userGuide.editorValidNoteDesc: Validation runs in a Web Worker to avoid blocking the interface, so there may be a slight delay.
userGuide.gramProcDesc: Procedures are the basic unit of the language. They are defined as follows:
userGuide.gramVarDesc: Variables are assigned using the assignment operator. Multiple notations are supported:
userGuide.gramVarImportantDesc: All assignments must end with a semicolon (;)
userGuide.gramStructImportantDesc: All control structures require BEGIN...END blocks or braces { }. Standalone statements are not allowed.
userGuide.gramPrintDesc: The print statement allows you to display values in the console:
userGuide.gramPrintExprDesc: You can include variables and mathematical operations
userGuide.gramPrintEscapeDesc: Use \" for quotes inside the string
userGuide.gramPrintNoteDesc: The cost of print is constant (O(1)) plus the cost of evaluating its arguments.
userGuide.analisisEditorDesc: In manual mode, you can write code directly in the editor and analyze it:
userGuide.analisisEditor1b: The editor validates syntax in real time
userGuide.analisisEditor2b: Use the "Verify Parse" button to validate syntax
userGuide.analisisEditor3b: Click "Analyze Complexity" to start the full analysis
userGuide.analisisEditor4b: The results page will open with cost table and detailed procedures
userGuide.analisisEditorTipDesc: If there are syntax errors, wait 3 seconds and an "AI Help" button will appear that will send your code to AALIE for automatic correction.
userGuide.analisisChatbotDesc: You can also analyze code directly from AALIE:
userGuide.analisisChatbot1b: Request an algorithm or paste code in the chat
userGuide.analisisChatbot2b: When AALIE returns code in a pseudocode block, a green "Analyze" button will appear next to the copy button
userGuide.analisisChatbot3b: The analysis runs directly in the chat view with the same loader as the manual editor
userGuide.analisisChatbot4b: When the analysis completes, it automatically navigates to the results page
userGuide.analisisChatbotAdvDesc: You can ask AALIE for corrections and analyze the corrected code without leaving the chat.
userGuide.analisisResultDesc: Once the analysis is complete, you will see:
userGuide.analisisResult1b: Shows elemental cost (Cₖ), number of executions and total cost per line
userGuide.analisisResult2b: In the top right corner, switch between Best/Average/Worst case
userGuide.analisisResult3b: Three cards show asymptotic notation (Big-O) for each case, with "View Procedure" buttons on each card
userGuide.analisisResult4a: General procedure: Click "View Procedure" on any card to see the full analysis
userGuide.analisisResult4b: Procedure per line: Click any line in the table to see the specific steps for that line
userGuide.bestCaseDesc: Analyzes the best case of the algorithm, considering:
userGuide.bestCase1: IF branches with fewer lines of code
userGuide.bestCaseExDesc: In linear search, the best case is O(1) if the element is in the first position.
userGuide.worstCaseDesc: Analyzes the worst case of the algorithm, considering:
userGuide.worstCase1: IF branches with more lines of code
userGuide.worstCaseExDesc: In linear search, the worst case is O(n) if the element does not exist or is at the end.
userGuide.avgCaseDesc: Analyzes the average case using probabilistic models:
userGuide.avgCase1: Uniform Model: Uniform probability distribution (p = 1/2 by default)
userGuide.avgCaseExDesc: In linear search, the average case is O(n/2) ≈ O(n) assuming uniform distribution.
userGuide.analisisResultNoteDesc: Procedures show detailed steps in LaTeX, from the original expression to the final polynomial form and asymptotic notation. For average case, A(n) is shown instead of T(n).
userGuide.analisisLlmDesc: The system allows comparing the automatic analysis with an independent analysis generated by an LLM (Gemini 2.5 Pro):
userGuide.analisisLlm1b: The LLM analyzes the code without knowing the system result
userGuide.analisisLlm2b: Compares both analyses and detects discrepancies
userGuide.analisisLlm3b: Generates a brief note (≤100 characters) indicating whether the analysis is correct
userGuide.analisisLlmNoteDesc: AI functions (such as LLM comparison) require a Gemini API key. You can configure it in the application footer.
userGuide.analisisGpuDesc: The system analyzes whether your algorithm is more suitable for GPU or CPU through a scoring system (0-100):
userGuide.analisisTraceDesc: The system allows you to visualize the step-by-step execution of your algorithm with specific input values:
userGuide.analisisTraceIter1: Instruments the code to capture state at each step
userGuide.analisisTraceIter2: Shows variable values at each iteration
userGuide.analisisTraceIter3: Visualizes execution flow with React Flow
userGuide.analisisTraceRec1: Generates recursive call tree diagram with LLM (Gemini 2.0 Flash)
userGuide.analisisTraceRec2: Shows recursive calls with input/output values
userGuide.analisisTraceRec3: Visualizes the complete tree with React Flow
userGuide.analisisTraceRec4: Includes explanation of the recursion process
userGuide.analisisTraceNoteDesc: AI functions (such as recursive diagram generation) require a Gemini API key. Iterative tracing does not require an API key.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy - AALIE
privacy.heroDesc: Your privacy is our priority. This academic project requires no registration, stores no personal data, and processes your code temporarily.
privacy.card3Item3: External AI for AALIE, comparison and diagrams (Gemini)
privacy.faq1A: No. Your code is processed temporarily in memory and automatically deleted when the analysis is complete.
privacy.faq2Q: Do I need to create an account?
privacy.faq2A: No. The service works completely without registration. We do not request any personal data.
privacy.faq3Q: Do you use external AI services?
privacy.faq3A: Yes, we use Google Gemini for three specific features: (1) General assistance AALIE, (2) Analysis comparison with LLM (Gemini 2.5 Pro), and (3) Diagram generation for recursive algorithms (Gemini 2.0 Flash). The main complexity analysis is performed entirely with our own backend (FastAPI + ANTLR4 + SymPy) without AI. Data sent to Gemini is processed according to Google's privacy policy.
privacy.faq4Q: How is my Gemini API Key handled?
privacy.faq4A: If you provide your own Gemini API Key, it is stored only locally in your browser (localStorage). It is not sent or stored on our servers. The API key is used directly from your browser for calls to Gemini API (AALIE, LLM comparison, recursive diagrams). We recommend using API keys with limited permissions and monitoring their use in Google Cloud Console. You can remove your API key at any time from the application footer.
privacy.faq5A: Only minimal server logs (IP, User-Agent, timestamps) for service diagnostics and monitoring. They are not linked to identities nor used commercially. AALIE messages and code sent for comparison/diagrams may be processed by Gemini API according to Google's terms of service. We do not store analysis history or processed code.
privacy.faq6Q: Is it safe to analyze sensitive code?
privacy.faq6A: The main complexity analysis is processed temporarily without storage. However, if you use LLM features (AALIE, comparison, recursive diagrams), your code may be sent to Gemini API. Avoid sending critical information, passwords, secrets or sensitive data. For confidential code, use only basic analysis without AI features.
privacy.faq7A: For any privacy inquiries, suggestions or issues, you can contact us:
